reason: The cited lines read commit history from a Git repository and return it to the agent, including commit hashes, authors, dates, and messages, so they establish returning repository/host data (SECRET). Commit authors/messages/subjects are repository-controlled content and can be attacker-controlled in a repo, so UNTRUSTED is supported. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution; they invoke Git log/read commits in a constrained way, not arbitrary code execution. They also do not send agent-supplied data to any attacker-readable external destination, so SINK is not supported.
